# Holiday rentals in Costa del Sol

Discover our luxury accommodation in Marbella and enjoy an unforgettable holidays.

In Marbella you will find culture, leisure and glamour. Come and discover one of the most exclusive cities in the Mediterranean, a true pride of the Costa del Sol. A city full of life, with twenty-eight kilometers of coastline, four marinas, the most select golf courses and a privileged climate, make it an incomparable destination.

Visiting our city will impress you. Endless activities, distinguished restaurants and beach clubs, sports of all kinds, endless possibilities that will make your trip a unique experience. The best and most luxurious accommodations will give the finishing touch to this perfect destination. Discover our selection and enjoy your vacation.

Nestled along the sun-drenched coastline of southern [Spain](https://www.solmarvillas.com/destinations/spain-villas), the Costa del Sol is a haven for those looking for sun, sea, and authentic cultural experiences. Known for its stunning beaches, vibrant nightlife, and charming Andalusian towns, this picturesque region invites you to explore its hidden gems. Our handpicked selection of Costa del Sol villas offers the perfect blend of comfort and style, providing an ideal retreat for relaxation and adventure.

#### More about Costa del Sol

Beaches in Costa del Sol

An infinite stretch of golden sand is what draws so many to a Costa del Sol villa holiday year after year, and the calming blue waters of the Mediterranean are the perfect backdrop. A wide selection of beach activities are available in the better-known resorts, including swimming, snorkelling and water sports.

Many beaches also hold the prestigious [Blue Flag status](https://www.blueflag.global/), making them safe for young swimmers, including a nine-kilometre stretch of sand in [Torremolinos](https://www.solmarvillas.com/destinations/spain-villas/mainland-spain/costa-del-sol/torremolinos) and five glorious beaches in [Marbella](https://www.solmarvillas.com/destinations/spain-villas/mainland-spain/costa-del-sol/marbella).

### Playa El Salon

There's nothing like this beautiful beach, which is the epitome of tranquillity and raw natural beauty. Located near Nerja Old Town, you can appreciate the rocky terrain and crystal-clear waters while sipping your favourite cocktail.

### Playa Las Viborillas

Another calming haven away from the hustle and bustle of vibrant clubs and bars is Playa Las Viborillas. The beach is full of natural beauty, with plenty of trees that offer shade and crystal blue waters.

### Playa de Burriana

Nerja is renowned for its beautiful sandy beaches, and this one certainly takes prime position. Plenty of activities are available, including pedalos, water sports and restaurants.

### Cabopino Beach

For a quieter vibe, this beach to the east of Marbella offers a more natural setting, backed by sand dunes and a protected area for those looking to escape the crowds.

### Playa de Maro

No visit to Costa del Sol is complete without discovering the hidden gem of Playa de Maro, just outside Nerja. Known for its dramatic cliffs and crystal-clear waters, it’s the perfect spot for snorkelling and exploring the underwater world.

Nightlife in Costa del Sol

Costa del Sol's nightlife varies from lively and fast-paced to more low-key and relaxing, depending on where you set your sights in the evenings.

Enjoy a slice of luxury at one of Marbella holiday villas. You'll be close to the chic marina, where the bars come alive at night, and mega yachts glisten in the bay.

For a more traditional Spanish evening, head to one of the mountain villages such as [Estepona](https://www.solmarvillas.com/destinations/spain-villas/mainland-spain/costa-del-sol/estepona) or Benahavis. Our holiday villas in Costa del Sol are ideally located so you can explore the Spanish nightlife scene.

### Torremolinos

In recent years, [Torremolinos](https://www.solmarvillas.com/destinations/spain-villas/mainland-spain/costa-del-sol/torremolinos) has transformed into one of the most vibrant nightlife hubs along Malaga’s coastline, particularly celebrated for its lively LGBTQ+ scene. Once a sleepy fishing village, this charming area now effortlessly blends its laid-back beach atmosphere with an energetic nightlife. By day, you can bask on some of the Costa del Sol’s finest beaches, and by night, the town comes alive with open-air beach clubs, drawing a diverse and lively crowd, particularly in the summer months.

While often considered a favourite among British tourists, more Spaniards are now flocking to Torremolinos to soak up its electric nightlife. Here, you can enjoy the perfect blend of sun, sea, and unforgettable evenings under the stars.

### Marbella

Along with its glitzy neighbor Puerto Banus, Marbella has become synonymous with luxury nightlife. This is the go-to spot if you enjoy stylish evenings, with late nights and a price tag to match—expect to spend more here than at any other location in the region. Two of the most iconic venues include the famous [Nikki Beach](https://marbella.nikkibeach.com/) resort, which kicks off the summer season at the end of April, and the [collection of bars along the renowned ‘Golden Mile’](https://marbslifestyle.com/blog/surroundings/golden-mile/).

Make sure to pay a visit to Marbella Old Town as well. It's a picturesque area that will undoubtedly earn a spot in your favourite holiday memories. Nestled in the heart of Marbella, just a short stroll from Venus Beach, it’s the perfect place for a leisurely post-dinner walk. It's dotted with quaint cafes and bars, all housed in beautifully preserved buildings that have stood for centuries. The cobblestone streets, lined with flower-adorned balconies, make for a peaceful stroll. With no cars allowed on the narrow streets, it’s a pedestrian’s paradise. If you’re driving, parking can be found nearby on Avenida del Mar.

### Nerja

If the glitzy, high-energy vibe of Marbella isn't quite your scene, head to the quaint fishing town of Nerja. Known for its relaxed atmosphere, beautiful beaches, and fresh seafood, [Nerja](https://www.solmarvillas.com/destinations/spain-villas/mainland-spain/andalucia/nerja) also offers a vibrant nightlife, especially for those who enjoy live music. The town’s lively bars and pubs, many clustered around the central square known as Plaza Tutti Frutti, provide one of the best live music experiences on the Andalusian coast. For an extra dose of local culture, plan your visit around early to mid-October, when Nerja’s annual fiesta takes place.

Food and Drink in Costa del Sol

The Costa del Sol is a culinary paradise, offering a delightful selection of dining options that reflect the region’s rich cultural heritage and bountiful local ingredients. From traditional tapas bars to fine dining establishments, the food scene here caters to every palate and preference.

Or if you want to enjoy a meal in the comfort of your own home, pick up local delicacies at a supermarket to enjoy alfresco back at your Costa del Sol villa!

### La Ola (Marbella)

This charming restaurant is a true coastal treasure, offering a distinctive dining experience with the gentle sounds of the sea as your backdrop. [La Ola Marbella's](https://www.instagram.com/laolamarbella/?hl=en-gb) menu is a delightful showcase of flavours, featuring dishes like artichoke hearts paired with jamón, spaghetti el pil pil, grilled octopus on skewers, a traditional fritura malagueña, and perfectly cooked rosada. And the attentive and friendly staff, headed by a gracious owner, create a warm and inviting atmosphere. Make sure to save room for dessert, as their tiramisu is a delightful surprise that you won't want to miss.

### Bamboleo (Mijas)

[Bamboleo](https://lazambrahotel.com/restaurants/bamboleo/) in [Mijas](https://www.solmarvillas.com/destinations/spain-villas/mainland-spain/costa-del-sol/mijas) ticks all the boxes for a truly special occasion. With a stunning terrace offering breathtaking views of the southern sunsets, along with a creative selection of signature cocktails and delicious bites, it’s a place that invites you to indulge. Named after the legendary Julio Iglesias, Bamboleo has become a favourite for those looking to embrace a carefree atmosphere and celebrate life in style.

### Bodega Charolais (Fuengirola)

This delightful spot in [Fuengirola](https://www.solmarvillas.com/destinations/spain-villas/mainland-spain/costa-del-sol/fuengirola) offers an experience filled with joy, from its spacious sun-drenched terrace, which is always in high demand, to its friendly staff (who will shower your little ones with affectionate attention). [Bodega Charolais](https://guide.michelin.com/gb/en/andalucia/fuengirola/restaurant/charolais) has a contemporary twist on traditional Spanish cuisine, and you can enjoy quality red or white wine by the glass, a refreshing change from the typical house offerings found elsewhere. It’s the kind of place you’ll find yourself dreaming about long after you leave.

### El Gato Lounge (Torremolinos)

[El Gato Lounge](https://www.instagram.com/el_gato_lounge/?hl=en-gb) is a gorgeous seaside restaurant on the [Torremolinos](https://www.solmarvillas.com/destinations/spain-villas/mainland-spain/costa-del-sol/torremolinos) promenade, offering an escape from the bustling streets of Málaga. Here, you can unwind with a glass of local sherry and a delicious platter of ham, cheese, and olives.

The menu features an extensive selection of cold tapas, along with enticing hot seafood specials and fusion dishes. Sample local favourites like boquerones (marinated anchovies) and fresh prawns, or enjoy classics like salmon tartar or a burger. With the soothing sound of the waves, it's the perfect spot to relax and indulge.

History and Culture in Costa del Sol

Our villas for rent in Costa del Sol have so much history and culture waiting on the doorstep.

### Alcazaba

In Málaga, the [Alcazaba](https://www.alcazabamalaga.com/) stands out, a Moorish fortress dating back to the 11th century with stunning views over the city and harbour.

### Museo Ralli

Another must-visit is the remarkable private art museum located just 6km west of central Marbella, near Puerto Banús. It offers an impressive collection of works from both Latin American and European artists. The bright, airy galleries showcase a diverse range of art, including sculptures by Salvador Dalí and vibrant surrealist paintings from Argentinian artist Alicia Carletti and Peruvian artist Herman Braun-Vega. With exhibitions that regularly rotate, it ensures a fresh and dynamic experience for art lovers.

### Marbella Old Town

The Old Town in Marbella is a charming labyrinth of narrow, cobbled streets lined with historic buildings, including the Church of Santa María and the Plaza de los Naranjos. Each of these landmarks paints a rich picture of Costa del Sol's layered history, making it a must-visit for history lovers.

Enjoy Nature and Wildlife

You get to appreciate golden beaches and friendly locals when you go to the Costa del Sol, and you also have plenty of nature and wildlife attractions to keep you busy. Animal lovers can head to the [Butterfly Park in Benalmadena](https://www.mariposariodebenalmadena.com/en/), the largest of its kind in Europe.

Alternatively, why not take a hike up El Cielo Mountain? It's a great way to take in the stunning scenery, or you can take it easy in one of Malaga's parks.

Make Costa del Sol Your Next Coastal Getaway

Whether you want to stay in La Cala de Mijas, Marbella, Torremolinos or [Estepona](https://www.solmarvillas.com/destinations/spain-villas/mainland-spain/costa-del-sol/estepona), we have a range of stunning villas in Costa del Sol. This picture-perfection region is famous for a reason, and our villas put you straight in the heart of the action.

### Family-friendly villas in Costa del Sol

If you're looking for a holiday home within walking distance to the beach bars, our Costa del Sol villas are in a perfect location. Most come with private pool amenities, air conditioning and WiFi.

You get all the creature comforts to enjoy whilst still being within reach of the many local attractions.

### Luxury villas with private pool facilities

Let’s not forget that Costa del Sol is also known for its [exceptional holiday homes](https://www.solmarvillas.com/villa-types/luxe-collection), attracting visitors eager to enjoy its renowned golf courses. Many of our villas in Costa del Dol have heated pools and can accommodate up to 10 guests, offering an experience like no other.

Escape to Endless Sunshine – Book Your Costa del Sol Villa Today

Nestled along the sun-soaked coast of southern Spain, our holiday villas in Costa del Sol offer an exquisite escape, where relaxation meets the region's rich heritage. Whether you're unwinding by your private pool or exploring the vibrant local culture, each villa serves as a gateway to the beauty and charm of this Mediterranean paradise.

With carefully curated comforts and prime locations, your stay promises to be a seamless blend of modern amenities and the timeless allure of the Costa del Sol. Embrace the opportunity to create lasting memories—your perfect retreat awaits.

For help planning your getaway, [contact our friendly team](https://www.solmarvillas.com/contact-us); we're here to help you find the perfect Costa del Sol villa for your dream holiday.

##### Visit southern Spain’s most spectacular cities







Granada is home to Spain’s most visited monument, The Alhambra. This impressive palace, surrounded by high walls, was the residence of the Nasrid sultans between the 13th and 15th centuries and is an absolute must when visiting the city. Seville, meanwhile, boasts some of the most stunning architecture in Europe, and the city can be admired from the famous ‘Metropol Parasol’, the tallest wooden structure in the world. Simply strolling through this remarkable city is entertainment in itself!

- ![Local Festivals](https://www.solmarvillas.com/sites/default/files/styles/image_414x260/public/local-festivals-costa-del-sol.png.webp?itok=LtrozMY7)





##### Local Festivals







Festivals, or ‘Fiestas’, in the Costa del Sol are hugely popular and form an important part of the culture of this wonderful region. Spain is a very religious country, so many of the festivals honour patron saints and other Catholic-Christian celebrations, complete with impressive costumes and parades through the streets. You can also enjoy an authentic taste of the flamboyant ‘Flamenco’ dance, which originated in Andalucia, with numerous shows held throughout the year.

- ![Indulge in Delicious Food](https://www.solmarvillas.com/sites/default/files/styles/image_414x260/public/local-cuisine-costa-del-sol.png.webp?itok=euDG9oP0)





##### Indulge in Delicious Food







When it comes to a villa holiday around the gorgeous Costa del Sol, there's nothing quite like trying all the local delicacies you can. From incredible iberico pork, tasty croquetas and even a delicious locally made wine or two, try something different every night or stick with the classics of paella and endless plates of tapas - the choice is yours!

## Costa del Sol Apartments - for sizzling sun, vibrant night life and fun activities for all your family and friends

Down in Andalucia, the weather here is balmy, and the region contains the city of Malaga, as well as iconic tourist destinations such as Torremolinos, Marbella and Nerja. The beach is obviously the big draw for many people heading out to stay in **Costa del Sol holiday villas**, as well as the excellent weather. The temperature here rarely drops below 15C, even at the peak of winter, and summer temperatures often exceed 38C. The harbour of Cabopino, close to Marbella, possess some of the best sands in Spain, and visitors can find shade from the excesses of the sun among its sand dunes and palm trees. Other excellent beaches include the Playa del Saladillo, near to Estepona, and Bounty Beach, again near Marbella.

## A holiday classic - stay in Villas in Costa del Sol for endless beach fun

Many groups of visitors who head to Costa del Sol holiday rentals are travelling to party. The area is especially popular with stag and hen parties, and the nightlife in coastal towns such as Torremolinos is usually very vibrant indeed. While the restaurants, bars and clubs in these coastal towns are often very lively, quieter places can be found in smaller towns, and Malaga is a big city with a lot of very different venues to offer. Eating out is a way of life in this part of Spain, and even the simplest ‘venta’ can offer superb food at great prices.

## Choose Costa del Sol Villa Rentals and enjoy the summer holiday of a lifetime

Golf is another activity which draws in thousands of visitors every year to the region. Indeed, some even refer to this part of Spain as the 'Costa del Golf'. The warm temperatures mean many golfers stay in Costa del Sol villa rentals during the winter months, especially if they are from northern Europe. There are 45 golf courses along the Costa del Sol, with many more nearby elsewhere in Andalucia. Four of the Costa del Sol courses are ranked in the top ten in Europe, making this a dream destination for anyone looking to tread in the footsteps of Seve Ballesteros. With great local produce ensuring that the food and wine is good and plentiful, this part of Spain can really offer almost anything anyone wants from a beach holiday. Staying in Costa del Sol holiday rentals provides access to some of Europe's best weather and beaches, while golfers will feel that have arrived in paradise.

- What attractions should you visit during a week-long stay in the Costa del Sol, Spain?



A week in the Costa del Sol allows for a taste of its diverse offerings. You could explore Malaga, visiting the Alcazaba fortress, Picasso Museum, and the Cathedral. Then, head to Marbella, known for its glamorous Puerto Banús marina. A day trip to Ronda, with its dramatic Puente Nuevo bridge and stunning views, is a must. Consider visiting the charming white villages of the interior, like Mijas, offering beautiful views and traditional Andalusian architecture. For beach time, enjoy the sands of Torremolinos or Fuengirola.

- What are the best short term rentals in Costa del Sol?





Among the short term rentals in Costa del Sol, [Salon Con Vistas Al Tajo](https://www.cozycozy.com/us/costa-del-sol-short-term-rentals#cp:details/47035570), [Apartamentos Turísticos Espinel](https://www.cozycozy.com/us/costa-del-sol-short-term-rentals#cp:details/236294) and [Apartamento Los Remedios 36 Bajo](https://www.cozycozy.com/us/costa-del-sol-short-term-rentals#cp:details/39391041) are the most popular ones.

- What attractions should you visit when you spend a month in the Costa del Sol, Spain?



A month gives you ample time for a deeper exploration. Beyond the highlights mentioned above, delve into the region's history with visits to Roman ruins like those in Baelo Claudia. Explore the natural beauty of El Torcal de Antequera, a stunning karst landscape. Consider a hike in the Sierra de las Nieves Natural Park, a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve. Take day trips to nearby cities like Seville or Granada, experiencing the Alhambra Palace. Enjoy the various beaches along the coast, from the lively shores of Benalmádena to the quieter coves near Nerja. Don't forget to spend time in smaller towns like Frigiliana, known for its charming streets and Moorish heritage.

- What are the best short term rentals with a pool in Costa del Sol?





[Apartamentos Cedro Alto](https://www.cozycozy.com/us/costa-del-sol-short-term-rentals#cp:details/27248549), [Apartamentos Avanel](https://www.cozycozy.com/us/costa-del-sol-short-term-rentals#cp:details/39904439) and [Macdonald Villacana Resort](https://www.cozycozy.com/us/costa-del-sol-short-term-rentals#cp:details/1456091) are the best short term rentals with a pool in Costa del Sol.

- Can visitors to the Costa del Sol, Spain witness any unique natural cycles, like cherry blossom season or autumn colors?



Yes, the Costa del Sol showcases seasonal changes. While not as dramatic as higher altitudes, you can enjoy almond blossom in early spring, particularly in the inland areas around Ronda. Autumn brings warmer colors to the Sierra de las Nieves mountains, offering lovely hiking opportunities. The region's mild climate means vibrant colors aren't as intense as in other parts of Europe.

- What are the best short term rentals with a jacuzzi in Costa del Sol?





The best short term rentals with a jacuzzi in Costa del Sol are [Macdonald Villacana Resort](https://www.cozycozy.com/us/costa-del-sol-short-term-rentals#cp:details/1456091), [Apartment With Terrace With Views And Jacuzzi](https://www.cozycozy.com/us/costa-del-sol-short-term-rentals#cp:details/46113698) and [Attic Jacuzzi With Views](https://www.cozycozy.com/us/costa-del-sol-short-term-rentals#cp:details/47066112).

- What are the most meaningful ways to engage with locals and discover the culture in the Costa del Sol, Spain?



To connect with locals, visit smaller, less touristy towns and villages. Try attending a local festival or feria – many towns have their own celebrations throughout the year. Take a cooking class to learn traditional Andalusian recipes. Visit a local market, like the Atarazanas Market in Malaga, to experience the daily life and interact with vendors. Learning a few basic Spanish phrases will greatly enhance your interactions.

- What are the best short term rentals for families and kids in Costa del Sol?





The best short term rentals for families and kids in Costa del Sol are [Apartamentos Turísticos Espinel](https://www.cozycozy.com/us/costa-del-sol-short-term-rentals#cp:details/236294), [Apartamento " A "Museo Casco Historico](https://www.cozycozy.com/us/costa-del-sol-short-term-rentals#cp:details/10009979) and [Apartamentos Rondacentro](https://www.cozycozy.com/us/costa-del-sol-short-term-rentals#cp:details/1348018).

- Are there any distinctive cultural activities or hands-on workshops in the Costa del Sol, Spain?



Absolutely! Many workshops offer hands-on experiences. You can learn flamenco dancing, pottery making, or traditional Andalusian crafts. Several places provide cooking classes focusing on local cuisine. Wine tasting tours in the region's vineyards are also popular, offering a chance to sample local wines and learn about the winemaking process.

- What are some secret spots or hidden treasures to visit in the Costa del Sol, Spain?



Some lesser-known gems include the Caminito del Rey, a thrilling walkway through a gorge (reservations are essential). The dolmens of Antequera, ancient megalithic structures, offer a glimpse into prehistory. Explore the less-crowded beaches near Nerja, like Cala de Maro. Discover the charming village of Gaucín, perched high in the mountains, with breathtaking views.

- What should not be left out of your suitcase if you are going to the Costa del Sol, Spain?



Pack light, comfortable clothing suitable for warm weather, including swimwear. Don't forget sunscreen, a hat, and sunglasses for sun protection. Comfortable walking shoes are a must, especially if you plan on exploring the hills and towns. A reusable water bottle is essential, and an adapter for electronic devices might be needed.

- What are the most popular festivals in the Costa del Sol, Spain?



The Costa del Sol hosts numerous festivals throughout the year. The Feria de Malaga is a major event, featuring flamenco dancing, traditional food, and vibrant celebrations. Many towns and villages hold their own smaller ferias, offering a taste of local culture. Semana Santa (Holy Week) processions are also significant, with elaborate floats and religious fervor.

- Where should you try the best local food in the Costa del Sol, Spain?



For authentic Andalusian cuisine, explore smaller, family-run restaurants away from the main tourist areas. The Atarazanas Market in Malaga offers a variety of fresh produce and seafood. Many restaurants in the white villages serve traditional dishes. Look for places specializing in espetos (grilled sardines), gazpacho (cold tomato soup), and pescaíto frito (fried fish).

## Travel guide

### Villas for rent in the Costa del Sol

Spain's Costa del Sol, otherwise known as ‘The Sunshine Coast’, is without doubt one of the most popular tourist destinations in the world. Belonging to Malaga Province, in the southern part of the Iberian peninsula, it is famous for its subtropical climate and Mediterranean charm. Averaging at 320 days of annual sunshine, this coastal paradise boasts 160km of fine sand beaches, ranging from luxury lounging spots to quiet coves. Inland, discover a varied landscape dotted with whitewashed towns, cliffs, ravines and exotic flora and fauna. From the UNESCO World heritage Site and otherworldly caves of Nerja to the coastal glamour of Marbella, this colourful region of Spain’s south is one of the most popular tourist destinations - and for good reason!

Whether you stay in one of our luxury beachfront villas with a private pool or spacious, family-friendly villas in the heart of the Costa del Sol, you’ll get to experience the best that this slice of coastal heaven has to offer, with a Clickstay home from home. Discover why the Costa del Sol represents the true essence of Spanish culture and explore a world of colourful fiestas, world-class beaches, opera and tapas, where the Andalucian atmosphere can be felt in the winding, cobbled lanes and alfresco restaurants. The Costa del Sol is also an ideal location for families, with its water worlds, theme parks and beaches with plenty of facilities.

The Costa del Sol offers plenty for families, with theme and water parks galore. Make a splash at Mijas Water Park and Aqualand Torremolinos, the most famous in Spain, boasting amazing slides and water shutes, wave pools and plenty of play islands. Tivoli World in Benalmádena is the largest theme park in the Costa del Sol and Bioparc Fuengirola is home to over 200 species of wildlife, with a recreated jungle zone and modern facilities. Fly over the beaches of Marbella with a flyboard at Funny Beach, or for a day of peace and tranquility head to Benalmádena Butterfly Park built in the style of a Thai temple, with its waterfalls and over 1,500 exotic species of butterfly.

Holiday alongside the rich and famous in glamorous Marbella, with its luxury yachts, exclusive nightclubs and stunning backdrop of the Sierra Blanca mountains, or get your cultural hit in vibrant Malaga, with its art museums and festivals. Or perhaps you’ll be lured by pretty, hilltop Mijas, with its views of North Africa in the distance. Maybe the Andalucian appeal and ritzy marina of family-friendly Benalmádena appeals to you. Don’t overlook Torremolinos, now a thriving Mediterranean resort town at the foot of the Mijas mountains, a world away from its tacky '70s reputation. But if you’re looking for the perfect mix of city and seaside charm, then Estepona and Nerja are for you.

Boasting over 120 beaches, the Costa del Sol stretches all the way from the Strait of Gibraltar to Granada Province, where it borders the Costa Tropical. Its 161 kilometres of sand is just as famous for its nightlife as it is for its beaches and golf courses. If the charming live music, bars and pubs of Nerja and Mijas aren’t enough, follow the party crowd at Marbella’s world-famous Puerto Banús. Popular with the young free and single are Malaga and Torremolinos, with their lively cosmopolitan atmosphere. Families will appreciate the quieter resorts of Fuengirola and Mijas, with plenty of authentic restaurants, flamenco shows and of course, their charming old towns.

The beaches of the Costa del Sol offer something for everybody, whether you want a lively urban beach to people watch, secluded swimming bay, water sports hub or pristine, family-friendly Blue Flag spot to relax on. With long hot summers blending into the mildest of winters, they are there to enjoy year-round. Our holiday rentals in the Costa del Sol put you at the heart of it all. Malaga Airport is the main transit hub but there are three other airports within driving distance of the Costa del Sol; Gibraltar (70km south), Granada (191km north) and Jerez (177km east), which all offer direct flights from the UK, with taxi, bus and car hire services available.

### Key holiday info

- Malaga is the only airport in the Costa del Sol, with direct flights to the UK typically taking 2hrs 40 mins.
- The average daytime temperature in summer is 26°C, with an average of 14°C in winter.
- The sea temperature from July-September can reach 23°C.
- The Costa del Sol boasts 23 Blue Flag beaches.
- There are 5 natural parks in the Costa del Sol; Montes de Malaga, Sierra Bermeja Royals, Sierra de las Nieves, Sierra de Grazalema and the Tejada, Almijara and Alhama mountain ranges.
- The Costa del Sol is a top European destination for golf lovers, often dubbed as 'The Costa del Golf' boasting over 60 modern golf courses!

### Where to go in Costa del Sol

#### Marbella

Enjoy the high life under the Mediterranean sun from one of our premium holiday rentals and experience the full offerings of Spain’s most glamorous resort; Michelin star restaurants a subtropical climate, fabulous beaches, world-class nightlife and luxury boutiques.

#### Estepona

Stay in one of our holiday rentals in Estepona to enjoy its perfect blend of modern city living with traditional seaside charm. Discover a stylish marina with lively Spanish bars and authentic restaurants, and an old town with a cluster of quaint shops and bodegas.

#### Málaga

As one of Spain’s most desirable cultural, gastronomic and leisure destinations, Malaga is the perfect destination to experience the best of Spain. Rent one of our properties and take in its vibrant energy that can be felt from the golden beaches to the charming streets of the old town.

#### Mijas

Nestled in the mountainside, Mijas is a modern coastal resort with a lively residential area that still retains that traditional Spanish village feel. Our Mijas properties are a perfect base to bask in the sun on the beaches along its coast and explore Malaga's vast mountain region.

#### Benalmádena

Benalmádena is renowned for its sandy beaches, but there is far more to this stunning town than its pristine coast. Our holiday rentals in Benalmádena put you at the heart of it all; the traditional old village, historic monuments and excellent restaurants.

#### Nerja

Famous for its Andalucian charm, subtropical climate, beaches and cosmopolitan atmosphere, Nerja is a great holiday destination. Our properties offer easy access to its historic town centre with its whitewashed houses, golden coastline and varied mountain landscape.

- Kids will love Selwo Aventura wildlife park, 15 minutes from Estepona and Torremolinos' Bateria Park, the largest in Spain, with its impressive playground and pool.
- The Costa del Sol is home to many world-class golf courses; the most famous being Real Club Valderrama and Sotogrande.
- Malaga city has over 30 museums; more museums than any other city in Andalucia.

## Discover Costa del Sol

Take a look at our blog posts about where to go in Costa del Sol and what to do on your holiday in Costa del Sol.

web.markdown:
# Villa Costa del Sol

Europe / Spain / Marbella

From its prestigious hilltop situation 3 km away from Estepona, at the centre of Marbella's golf district this grand property with private pool, gym, sauna and putting green is surrounded by fabulous landscaped gardens overlooking the sea and the Costa del Sol all the way to Gibraltar.

## Villa Overview

Up to8Guests

Up to4Bedrooms

6Bathrooms

from7Min. Nights

The beach is only 4 km away which makes this villa an excellent choice for a family beach holiday removed from the hustle and bustle of the coastal resorts. This property provides plenty of space for entertainment for the whole family, making the most of the splendid natural surroundings and the Andalusian sunshine. Active types will love swimming against the current, practicing golf, working out in the gym or playing a match of paddle before relaxing in the Jacuzzi and the sauna. Guests can also enjoy their meals al fresco under the pergola while soaking up the breath-taking panorama.

### Accommodations

#### Ground Floor

- Elegant living area, several sofas, fireplace, large flat screen TV, marble floors, doors to vast patio area with pool and sea views
- Arched door to dining area, desk and chair, views
- Large fully equipped, traditional-style kitchen, door to utility room and to side garden
- Gym room, treadmill, elliptical bike, some weights, yoga mats
- Guest WC
- Bedroom 2: Double size bed, en-suite bathroom, door to large covered terrace
- Bedroom 3: Double size bed, en-suite bathroom, door to large covered terrace
- Bedroom 4: Twin beds, en-suite bathroom

#### First Floor

- Bedroom 1: Master Suite, vanity area, large en-suite bathroom with a double jacuzzi and walk-in rain shower, door to terrace

#### Grounds

- Splendid manicured garden comprising mature trees and ample lawn areas, orchard with fruit trees (orange, mandarin, pink grapefruit, lemon, lime, figs, pomegranate, and olive trees)
- Covered terrace
- Large private 15m x 6m pool (Roman steps), built-in seating area with 3 Jacuzzi jets, jet-stream
- Breath-taking sea views
- Outdoor kitchen/ entertainment area, large pergola, al fresco dining facilities, BBQ, private Bar, Phillips beer tap and ice cube machine, pool table
- Bathroom, WC, small corner shower
- Sauna, covered terrace, hammock, additional seating
- Private golf area with a 9-hole putting green, private paddle court with views to La Concha mountain and the sea (necessary equipment to play is provided, just bring your own balls)
- Automated entrance gates, vast paved driveway, feature fountain
- Manicured gardens
- Double garage and ample parking on the driveway

Get to know Costa Del Sol

# **Luxury Villa Rentals in Costa del Sol, Spain**

Explore our [portfolio of luxury villa rentals in Costa del Sol](https://amaselections.com/magazine/a-m-a-selections-now-in-costa-del-sol), which offers a curated selection for you to choose from to experience the area with your friends and family in 2026. Our Costa del Sol villas have incredible amenities including private pools, exceptional Mediterranean sea views, outdoor dining areas for al fresco meals and exotic gardens. Whether you’re looking for a modern holiday villa with close access to the beach or a traditional finca that is authentic in design and bohemian in style, we can help you find the perfect vacation rental for your stay. If you are travelling with young children, we can advise you on the best child-friendly villas. Our family villas are set on the beautiful coast or near one of the many golf courses, allowing you to select the location that is better suited to your holiday preferences. In addition, you can explore our portfolio of private villas in Costa del Sol for large groups.

Costa del Sol, the “sunshine coast”, is comprised of [coastal towns](https://amaselections.com/magazine/these-are-the-must-visit-towns-of-costa-del-sol) and communities along the coastline of the province of Malaga in southern Spain. This region has become one of the top destinations for discerning travelers from England, Europe and beyond. Although famous for its beautiful stretch of sandy [beaches](https://amaselections.com/magazine/best-beach-clubs-marbella-spain), this region offers so much more. There is a wide array of [highly rated restaurants](https://amaselections.com/magazine/marbella-top-michelin-restaurant-guide) to choose from as well as local seafood restaurants and great brunch spots. There is a large diversity in landscapes including [beaches](https://amaselections.com/magazine/best-beach-clubs-marbella-spain), cliffs, estuaries, bays and dunes. From [charming villages](https://amaselections.com/magazine/these-are-the-must-visit-towns-of-costa-del-sol) to bustling nightlife and beautiful nature to a [fantastic food scene](https://amaselections.com/magazine/like-a-local-taste-your-way-through-costa-del-sol), Costa del Sol has all of the elements for an unforgettable holiday.
